# The data-stage acceptance golden, one line per engine:
#
#     <engine>  <sha256 of `jq -S .` over data-raw-dump.json>  <the mod set>
#
# Written and checked by scripts/run-datastage.sh, which packages
# guest/{go,rust}/examples/datastage as a mod, runs `factorio --dump-data`, and
# hashes the normalised dump.
#
# WHY NORMALISED. Key order in the dump is INSERTION order, so two mods
# differing only in the order they call data:extend produce dumps that differ at
# a byte and describe the same game. `jq -S` sorts every object; measured, that
# removes an ordering difference completely and preserves a real field-value
# change.
#
# WHY THE MOD SET IS HERE. The dump is a function of every mod that ran, and
# Factorio's bundled DLC data loads whatever --mod-directory says -- so a
# machine that owns different DLC produces a different dump for a mod that is
# perfectly fine. Recorded so a mismatch names its own cause and reads as SKIP
# rather than as a broken mod.
#
# WHY PER ENGINE. base's own prototypes move between series, so a hash taken on
# one engine says nothing about another. Both 2.0.x and 2.1.x are recorded, and
# the mod-set column is what makes the difference legible rather than mysterious:
# 2.1 bundles `recycler` and 2.0.77 does not.
2.0.77  b2f94000d43cedff88af03686774d182883feccba977c27836efcc8cd4e0907c  base@2.0.77 core@0.0.0 elevated-rails@2.0.77 fkd-example@0.1.0 quality@2.0.77 space-age@2.0.77
2.1.16  d7a87af89e4bb773c60fb6ef690cc6bb202f00beaf892e9f889db57ad2f3a3af  base@2.1.16 core@0.0.0 elevated-rails@2.1.16 fkd-example@0.1.0 quality@2.1.16 recycler@2.1.16 space-age@2.1.16
2.1.17  4bf04000445104978fb4f843ce20d8d6e3a93d2b9217e2e6f4f94c4d6ddc311b  base@2.1.17 core@0.0.0 elevated-rails@2.1.17 fkd-example@0.1.0 quality@2.1.17 recycler@2.1.17 space-age@2.1.17
